marketplace.name: infinia
marketplace.title: Infinia Xailon Marketplace
marketplace.description: Curated MCP servers, skills, recipes and mods for Xailon, each pinned to a reviewed commit.

items.name: github
items.title: GitHub
items.summary: Issues, pull requests, code search and Actions on GitHub.

env.GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: A fine-grained personal access token with the repository scopes you want the agent to use.

items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  github:
    type: stdio
    name: github
    cmd: docker
    args: [run, -i, --rm, -e, GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:v1.14.0]
    env_keys: [GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: playwright
items.title: Playwright
items.summary: Drive a real browser: navigate, click, fill forms and read pages through accessibility snapshots.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  playwright:
    type: stdio
    name: playwright
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@playwright/mcp@0.0.83"]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: context7
items.title: Context7
items.summary: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation pulled into the prompt.
items.configSnippet:

    name: context7
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@upstash/context7-mcp@4.1.1"]

items.name: filesystem
items.title: Filesystem
items.summary: Read, write and search files inside the directories you allow.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:

items.name: chrome-devtools
items.title: Chrome DevTools
items.summary: Drive and inspect a live Chrome: navigate, click, fill forms, read console and network, take screenshots, record performance traces.
items.notes: Requires Node ^20.19 || ^22.12 || >=23 and a local Chrome install; launches its own Chrome profile by default. Exposes browser content to the agent.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  chrome-devtools:
    type: stdio
    name: chrome-devtools
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, chrome-devtools-mcp@1.10.1]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: supabase
items.title: Supabase
items.summary: Manage Supabase projects: list projects, run SQL, apply migrations, inspect tables, logs, edge functions and config
items.notes: The hosted server is Supabase's documented primary path; the repo README no longer documents an npx stdio launch. It uses OAuth 2.1 on first use, where you pick the organisation. The URL accepts query options such as project_ref=<ref> and read_only=true to scope access; consider read_only for safety. Read Supabase's MCP security guidance on prompt injection through database contents. The source is
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  supabase:
    type: streamable_http
    name: supabase
    uri: https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: notion
items.title: Notion
items.summary: Search a Notion workspace and read, create and edit pages and databases in Markdown.
items.notes: OAuth on first use and respects the user's Notion permissions. The local makenotion/notion-mcp-server (MIT, npm @notionhq/notion-mcp-server 2.5.2) states in its README that it is no longer actively maintained and points users to the remote server, so it was not chosen. SSE fallback: https://mcp.notion.com/sse.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  notion:
    type: streamable_http
    name: notion
    uri: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: atlassian
items.title: Atlassian
items.summary: Search, read, create and update Jira issues and Confluence pages, plus other Atlassian Cloud products.
items.notes: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server, Atlassian Cloud only. OAuth on first use. The GitHub repo (Apache-2.0) holds docs and skills, not server source. The legacy /v1/sse endpoint is no longer supported after 30 June 2026.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  atlassian:
    type: streamable_http
    name: atlassian
    uri: https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: linear
items.title: Linear
items.summary: Find, create and update Linear issues, projects, cycles and comments.
items.notes: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration on first use. Alternatively send a Linear API key as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. A read-only endpoint exists at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  linear:
    type: streamable_http
    name: linear
    uri: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: sentry
items.title: Sentry
items.summary: Look up Sentry issues, events, stack traces, releases and projects in your organization.
items.notes: OAuth on first use. Can be scoped by path: /mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}. The source (getsentry/sentry-mcp, npm @sentry/mcp-server 0.42.0, stdio for self-hosted Sentry) is FSL-1.1-ALv2, which is outside the allowed licences, so only the hosted endpoint is listed.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  sentry:
    type: streamable_http
    name: sentry
    uri: https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: stripe
items.title: Stripe
items.summary: Search and call Stripe API methods (customers, payments, invoices, subscriptions, refunds) and search Stripe docs
items.notes: The hosted server is Stripe's documented primary path; the MCP server source is no longer in stripe/ai. It uses OAuth on first use and lets you grant access per live account or sandbox. Without OAuth, send an Agent API key as an Authorization: Bearer header. From 2026-10-31, full-access secret keys and non-Agent restricted keys are rejected. Some write actions, such as refunds and outbound payment
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  stripe:
    type: streamable_http
    name: stripe
    uri: https://mcp.stripe.com
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: figma
items.title: Figma (Framelink)
items.summary: Fetch Figma file and frame layout, styles and components as compact context, and download images, to implement designs in code.

env.FIGMA_API_KEY: Figma personal access token from Settings -> Security -> Personal access tokens (file content read scope)

items.notes: Figma's official remote server (https://mcp.figma.com/mcp) only accepts clients listed in Figma's MCP Catalog, so Xailon cannot use it unless listed. The official desktop server (http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp) needs the Figma desktop app with Dev Mode. For both reasons this entry uses the most-used community server (Framelink, about 16k stars, actively maintained). Reviewer may swap in the official en
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  figma:
    type: stdio
    name: figma
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, figma-developer-mcp@0.13.2, --stdio]
    env_keys: [FIGMA_API_KEY]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: slack
items.title: Slack
items.summary: Read Slack channels, threads and DMs, search messages, list users and channels; posting is opt-in per channel

env.SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN: Slack user OAuth token (xoxp-...) from a Slack app you install in your workspace, with the user scopes listed in the repo's docs/01-authentication-setup.md

items.notes: Why this server: the reference @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack is deprecated on npm and archived. Slack's own server is hosted only (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp, docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server). It requires confidential OAuth from a registered, directory-published or internal Slack app with a fixed client_id and client_secret, so a generic dynamic-registration client cannot use it; only partn
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  slack:
    type: stdio
    name: slack
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, slack-mcp-server@1.3.0, --transport, stdio]
    env_keys: [SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: postgres
items.title: PostgreSQL
items.summary: Inspect PostgreSQL schemas, run SQL, and check queries, indexes, locks and database health.

env.POSTGRES_HOST: Database host name or IP, e.g. localhost
env.POSTGRES_DATABASE: Name of the database to connect to
env.POSTGRES_USER: Database user (a read-only role is safest)

items.notes: Replaces the archived reference server in modelcontextprotocol/servers. This is Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases (Apache-2.0, ~16.6k stars, active), using its prebuilt postgres toolset; it is not from the PostgreSQL project. The npm package downloads the toolbox binary. SQL execution is not restricted to reads, so use a read-only role if needed. crystaldba/postgres-mcp (MIT) was considered, but
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  postgres:
    type: stdio
    name: postgres
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@toolbox-sdk/server@1.13.1", --prebuilt=postgres, --stdio]
    env_keys: [POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_DATABASE, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: fetch
items.title: Fetch
items.summary: Fetch a URL and return it as Markdown for the model to read.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  fetch:

    name: fetch
    cmd: uvx

    enabled: true

items.name: git
items.title: Git
items.summary: Inspect and operate on a local git repository: status, diff, log, branches and commits.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  git:
    type: stdio
    name: git
    cmd: uvx
    args: [mcp-server-git==2026.8.18]
    enabled: true

items.name: serena
items.title: Serena
items.summary: Semantic code navigation and editing via language servers: find symbols, references and insert or replace code by symbol
items.notes: LICENCE: v1.7.0 is the last MIT release. On 2026-09-06 (commit 6707cd9b) the repo relicensed the Serena application to GPL-3.0-or-later for v2; the change is not retroactive and the maintainers state all releases up to v1.7.0 / tag mit-final (74c38a65) remain MIT. The repo-level SPDX now reads NOASSERTION, and LICENSE at the v1.7.0 tag is plain MIT. Do NOT bump past v1.7.0 without re-checking the
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  serena:
    type: stdio
    name: serena
    cmd: uvx
    args: [--from, git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@949a27ef1e5fda1a6e7b561e777bcece345c6ffd, serena, start-mcp-server, --context=ide, --project-from-cwd]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: desktop-commander
items.title: Desktop Commander
items.summary: Run terminal commands and long-lived processes, manage processes, and search, read and edit local files.
items.notes: Gives the agent unrestricted shell and filesystem access as the user. Sends limited pseudonymous telemetry by default (no file contents, paths or command arguments); can be disabled via its set_config_value tool (telemetryEnabled=false).
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  desktop-commander:
    type: stdio
    name: desktop-commander
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander@0.2.52"]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: shadcn
items.title: shadcn/ui
items.summary: Browse, search and add shadcn/ui components and blocks from configured registries into the current project
items.notes: Launched through the shadcn CLI's mcp subcommand (ui.shadcn.com/docs/mcp). Works on a project with components.json. Private registries can need tokens such as REGISTRY_TOKEN set in .env.local, as defined by that registry's config. No env is needed for the public registry.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  shadcn:
    type: stdio
    name: shadcn
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, shadcn@4.21.1, mcp]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: terraform
items.title: Terraform
items.summary: Look up Terraform Registry providers, modules and policies with docs; optionally manage HCP Terraform or TFE workspaces
items.notes: Needs Docker. Public registry tools need no credentials. For the HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise tools, add -e TFE_TOKEN -e TFE_ADDRESS to the docker args and set TFE_TOKEN (API token) and TFE_ADDRESS (for example https://app.terraform.io) in the environment. Licence is MPL-2.0 (allowed).
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  terraform:
    type: stdio
    name: terraform
    cmd: docker
    args: [run, -i, --rm, hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server:1.3.0]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: n8n
items.title: n8n
items.summary: Look up n8n node docs and templates, and validate, create, update and run workflows on an n8n instance.

env.N8N_API_URL: Base URL of your n8n instance, e.g. https://n8n.example.com (only needed for workflow management tools)
env.N8N_API_KEY: n8n API key from Settings > n8n API (only needed for workflow management tools)

items.notes: Community server, not by n8n GmbH (~23k stars, commits daily). MCP_MODE, LOG_LEVEL and DISABLE_CONSOLE_OUTPUT are fixed values from the upstream stdio config, and stdout logging would corrupt the protocol. Documentation and validation tools work without N8N_API_URL/N8N_API_KEY. n8n itself offers an instance-level MCP endpoint, but its URL differs per instance.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  n8n:
    type: stdio
    name: n8n
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, n8n-mcp@2.91.0]
    envs:
      MCP_MODE: stdio
      LOG_LEVEL: error
      DISABLE_CONSOLE_OUTPUT: "true"
    env_keys: [N8N_API_URL, N8N_API_KEY]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: tavily
items.title: Tavily
items.summary: Web search, page extraction, site crawl and site map tools backed by the Tavily search API
items.notes: Tavily also hosts https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp, which takes the key as a ?tavilyApiKey= query parameter or uses OAuth. The local stdio launch was chosen so the key stays in an env var. Usage counts against Tavily API credits, with a free tier. Optional: DEFAULT_PARAMETERS (JSON of default search params) and TAVILY_HUMAN_ID.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  tavily:
    type: stdio
    name: tavily
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, tavily-mcp@0.2.22]
    env_keys: [TAVILY_API_KEY]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: apify

items.summary: Search and run Apify Actors to scrape websites, social media, maps and search engines, and fetch their results and docs.
items.notes: Vendor recommends the hosted server (it has features stdio lacks). OAuth on first use, or header 'Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>'. Running Actors consumes Apify credits. Local alternative: npx -y @apify/actors-mcp-server@0.17.2 with APIFY_TOKEN. The /sse endpoint has been removed.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  apify:
    type: streamable_http
    name: apify
    uri: https://mcp.apify.com
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: sequential-thinking
items.title: Sequential Thinking

items.name: docker-toolkit
items.title: Docker MCP Toolkit
items.summary: Single gateway to the MCP servers enabled in Docker's MCP Toolkit, each run in an isolated container with managed secrets.
items.notes: Uses the vendor-documented 'docker mcp gateway run' CLI plugin, which ships with Docker Desktop (or is installed from docker/mcp-gateway releases); its version is set by that install, not by these args. Enable servers first in Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit or with 'docker mcp server enable'. A container launch (docker/mcp-gateway:v0.44.1 with the Docker socket and ~/.docker/mcp mounted) is possible
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  docker-toolkit:
    type: stdio
    name: docker-toolkit
    cmd: docker
    args: [mcp, gateway, run]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: chrome
items.title: Chrome MCP (mcp-chrome)
items.summary: Control your everyday Chrome via an extension: tabs, navigation, clicks, forms, screenshots, network capture, history and bookmarks.
items.notes: Community project (Chrome has no vendor equivalent besides chrome-devtools). Prerequisites: install the mcp-chrome Chrome extension from the GitHub releases, then 'npm install -g mcp-chrome-bridge@1.0.31' (or 'mcp-chrome-bridge register') so the extension can start the native host, and click Connect in the extension. The stdio launcher proxies to the native host at http://127.0.0.1:12306/mcp (the
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  chrome:
    type: stdio
    name: chrome
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, -p, mcp-chrome-bridge@1.0.31, mcp-chrome-stdio]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: airtable
items.title: Airtable
items.summary: Read and write Airtable bases: list bases and tables, query and filter records, create, update and delete records, edit schema.
items.notes: Official hosted server, available on all plans. OAuth on first use; alternatively send 'Authorization: Bearer <personal access token>' with a PAT from https://airtable.com/create/tokens. Capabilities follow the user's base role. A popular unofficial local alternative is npm airtable-mcp-server 1.14.0 (domdomegg/airtable-mcp-server, MIT, needs AIRTABLE_API_KEY).
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  airtable:
    type: streamable_http
    name: airtable
    uri: https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: hubspot
items.title: HubSpot
items.summary: Search, read, create and update HubSpot CRM records such as contacts, companies, deals and tickets.
items.notes: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE only, no token path. HubSpot docs say generic clients must first create an MCP connector in the HubSpot account and use its Client ID and Client secret; dynamic client registration is not documented, so the client needs pre-registered OAuth client support. The local npm package @hubspot/mcp-server (MIT, token-based) is a beta last published 0.4.0 on 2025-06-18 and was not chose
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  hubspot:
    type: streamable_http
    name: hubspot
    uri: https://mcp.hubspot.com
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: metabase
items.title: Metabase
items.summary: Search Metabase dashboards, cards and databases, run saved questions and SQL queries, and export results.

env.METABASE_URL: Base URL of your Metabase instance, e.g. https://metabase.example.com
env.METABASE_API_KEY: Metabase API key from Admin > Settings > Authentication > API keys

This community server was chosen instead (MIT, ~90 stars, active). Read-only mode is on by default (METABASE_READ_ONLY_MODE=true). Email/password auth (METABASE_USER_
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  metabase:
    type: stdio
    name: metabase
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@jerichosequitin/metabase-mcp@1.1.7"]
    env_keys: [METABASE_URL, METABASE_API_KEY]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.title: Shopify Dev
items.summary: Search Shopify docs and API schemas, validate GraphQL, Liquid, theme and UI-extension code, and resolve API versions

It has no public source repo: github.com/Shopify/dev-mcp returns 404, so the gh api licence check could not be done; the related Shopify/Shopify-AI-Toolkit repo is MIT. Release builds send usage telemetry, including tool in
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  shopify-dev:
    type: stdio
    name: shopify-dev
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@shopify/dev-mcp@1.16.0"]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: stackoverflow
items.title: Stack Overflow
items.summary: Search Stack Overflow questions and fetch full questions, answers and comments by ID
items.notes: Hosted only, in beta, with OAuth through a Stack Exchange login on first use. Limited to 100 calls per day per user. The tools are so_search and get_content. The vendor docs configure it through npx mcp-remote mcp.stackoverflow.com rather than a direct http entry. The standard OAuth discovery documents (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and oauth-authorization-server) return 404 on mcp.stackov
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  stackoverflow:
    type: streamable_http
    name: stackoverflow
    uri: https://mcp.stackoverflow.com
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: ahrefs
items.title: Ahrefs
items.summary: Query Ahrefs SEO data: backlinks, keywords, site audit, rank tracking and Brand Radar.
items.notes: Requires a paid Ahrefs plan (Lite or higher). Auth via OAuth, or header 'Authorization: Bearer <MCP key>' using an MCP key generated under Account Settings -> API Keys (MCP keys differ from API v3 keys). The local npm server @ahrefs/mcp (github ahrefs/ahrefs-mcp-server) is archived and marked outdated by Ahrefs, so it is not used. Ahrefs terms forbid using the endpoint from custom scripts or bridg
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  ahrefs:
    type: streamable_http
    name: ahrefs
    uri: https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: ibkr
items.title: Interactive Brokers
items.summary: Read IBKR account balances, positions, trades and market data, search contracts and options, and draft order instructions.
items.notes: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + dynamic client registration; browser sign-in on first use; revoke in Client Portal > Settings > Manage Third-Party Consents. IBKR's WAF reportedly rejects OAuth discovery/registration requests without a User-Agent header. Trading tools draft order instructions and do not place orders on their own. https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/mcp also answers but the vendor guide for third-party
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  ibkr:
    type: streamable_http
    name: ibkr
    uri: https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/mcp-public
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.title: Sentry Issues
items.summary: Read-only inspection of Sentry issues and events with the sentry CLI: list recent errors, view events, run root-cause explain.

items.name: sentry-find-bugs
